# n10 - The wiring the review found missing

n9 closes the four blockers. What is left from `resources/review--post-execution-2026-09-11.md` is a
set of pieces that exist, are tested in isolation, and are never called; plus a set of reports that
say something the code did not do.

Three whole components have no production caller. `RunnerProposals` is validated by `NodeReturn`,
carried in every return, and then dropped on the floor, so D15's minted ids and refusal rules are
vacuously satisfied and n7's CHANGELOG line about them is untrue. `NodeWorktree.reap` is D26's
runner-owned reaper and runs nowhere. `--allow-core-drift` is D11's escape hatch, exists as a
keyword argument, and no flag reaches it, which is precisely why Plastic's own repository, whose
tree legitimately drifts from the installed manifest, cannot dogfood its own runner.

Two reports lie. The Status table renders a blocker string into every terminal node's Detail, so a
node that is `done` reads "n1 is done, not eligible to enter running". A step that dispatched
nothing because the concurrency ceiling was full reports `stalled`, which is the word for a graph
that cannot continue, not for one that is simply busy.

And one number is inert. A node's declared `budget:` reaches nothing: dispatch passes no budget,
the packet builder never reads the node block's own, and the ready-set loader does not carry it. A
node with a large body is not cut down, it is refused outright, and by the same review's M6 that
refusal prints nothing at all.
